message.content:
The most commonly cited figure for California’s residential market is the **median home value**, which is a good proxy for the “average” price people actually pay. According to Zillow’s latest data (mid‑2024):

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Median home value (California) | **≈ $800 000** |
| Median home value (Los Angeles) | ≈ $1 200 000 |
| Median home value (San Francisco) | ≈ $1 500 000 |
| Median home value (San Diego) | ≈ $850 000 |

If you’re looking for a true arithmetic mean (which is higher because of a few very expensive properties), the average is roughly **$850 000–$900 000**.  

So, a typical Californian home costs somewhere between **$800 k and $900 k**.
